name: UT-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Post-redistricting fundamentals strongly favor Democrats (PVI D+12)

McAdams has a massive financial edge: $2.3M raised and $2.7M outside support vs. under $150K for Owen
model.rationale: Fundamentals point decisively toward McAdams after redistricting, and both Kalshi and Polymarket price him near 96%. His overwhelming fundraising and outside-spending advantage against a barely funded opponent leaves little evidence to move from a roughly 21-point expected margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a closer race or a surge in Republican outside spending would be the first sign the margin is narrowing.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
This open seat was redrawn in a way that gives Democrats a clear structural edge, with a partisan lean of about 12 points and fundamentals pointing to a margin above 20. Ben McAdams enters as the strong favorite, having raised over $2.2 million and drawn $2.7 million in outside support, while Republican Riley Owen has raised roughly $133,000 with minimal cash on hand. No outside groups are spending against McAdams.

Prediction markets on both Kalshi and Polymarket price McAdams at about 96 percent, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. With no general-election polling available, the forecast rests on fundamentals and money, both of which point the same way. The race is rated Safe D, with modest residual uncertainty from the absence of polls.
